[[File:Turkmen Saryja Sheep Breed.jpg|thumb|Saryja Sheep Breed in Turkmenistan]]
'''Saryja''' (also: '''Saraja'''; [[Turkmen language|Turkmen]]: saryja goýuny) is a breed of fat-tailed [[sheep]] developed on the territory of [[Turkmenistan]]. The breed was developed through a long-term selection of Turkmen breeds of [[fat-tailed sheep]], which had a high content of fluff in [[wool]]. The breed received its name from the village of Saryja, located near the Turkmen city of [[Mary, Turkmenistan|Mary]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.agroxxi.ru/wiki-animal/ovcy/polugrubosherstnye-porody-ovec/saradzhinskaja-poroda-ovec.html|title=Сараджинская порода овец|author=Евгения Чернышова|website=AgroXXI|date=2014-02-03|access-date=2021-06-22|archive-date=2021-06-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624203850/https://www.agroxxi.ru/wiki-animal/ovcy/polugrubosherstnye-porody-ovec/saradzhinskaja-poroda-ovec.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

== About the breed ==
Sheep of the Saryja breed are usually white in color, while the legs and head are red. The musculature is poorly developed, and the coat is semi-coarse and shiny, contains a lot of fluff and contains almost no dead hair. [[Fleece (sheep)|Fleece]] is of braid structure, the length of braids is 13–18 cm and the fluff is 6–9 cm.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Batyrov |first=Seyitguly |date=2004-08-01 |title=Turkmen Saryja Wool: Basic Characteristics |url=https://www.jozan.net/turkmen-saryja-wool-basic-characteristics/ |access-date=2023-06-29 |website=JOZAN |language=en-US}}</ref>

The weight of an adult sheep is on average from 50 to 60 kg, the largest individuals reach 75 kg, the average weight of a ram is from 80 to 90 kg, and the largest reach 100 kg or more.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Batyrov |first=Seyitguly |date=2004-08-01 |title=Turkmen Saryja Wool: Basic Characteristics |url=https://www.jozan.net/turkmen-saryja-wool-basic-characteristics/ |access-date=2023-06-29 |website=JOZAN |language=en-US}}</ref>

Saryja sheep are hardy and well adapted to year-round keeping on pastures and with limited feeding in winter. It is considered one of the best fat-tailed breeds of meat and tallow. With the help of breeding rams of the Saryja breed, such breed groups of sheep as Tajik and Karagaly were developed.<ref name=":12">{{Cite web|url=http://www.cnshb.ru/AKDiL/0044/base/k0060032.shtm|title=Генетические ресурсы сельскохозяйственных животных в России и сопредельных странах|last1=Эрнст |first1=Л.К. |last2=Дмитриев |first2=Н.Г. |last3=Паронян |first3=И.А.|date=1994|location=Санкт-Петербург|publisher=ВНИИГРЖ|access-date=2021-06-23|archive-date=2021-06-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624204054/http://www.cnshb.ru/AKDiL/0044/base/k0060032.shtm|url-status=live}}</ref>

In [[Turkmenistan]], Saryja sheep are bred in the southern part of the central [[Karakum Desert|Karakum]], as well as on the plains adjacent to the [[Kopet Dag|Kopetdag Range]].<ref name=":12"/> Also, sheep of Saryja breed are grown in [[Kazakhstan]], [[Uzbekistan]] and [[Russia]] ([[Orenburg Oblast|Orenburg region]] and Altai).<ref name=":0" />
